text:
Alex W: FYI handing off for the afternoon shift. Short summary of the last 6h: we saw a spike of 429s for a subset of Dedicated tenants after a large background compaction kicked off on node pool-a. Root cause seems like aggressive KV cache eviction combined with queueing in the batcher, which cascaded into token-level throttles. :rotating_light:

incident-bot: INCIDENT #INC-2026-243 triggered 14:02 UTC — high 429 rate observed for /v1/generate on dedicated-nyc cluster. Pages sent to oncall@redwood. Severity: Sev2.

Alex W: What we did so far:
- Scoped impact: ~3 customers (dedicated tenants) experienced increased 429s for ~18m. Primary user impact: failed interactive generations and elevated latency.
- Short mitigation: scaled up pool-a by +2 GPUs and temporarily disabled the background compaction job for pool-a.
- Applied conservative KV cache size bump for the affected hosts (config: `kv.cache.max_entries=1_200_000 -> 1_800_000`).
- Enabled soft-fallback routing to model-variant `gptx-compact-v1` for failing requests.

Priya K: Current status: traffic back to normal for 2 tenants, one tenant still seeing intermittent 429s (~0.3% RPS). Metrics show KV eviction_rate spike coincident with compaction start at 13:58 UTC.

Mateo R: Logs from the batcher looked like this (snippet):
```
2026-03-13T13:59:01Z batcher warn: queue_latency=210ms pending=256 drop_rate=0.12
2026-03-13T13:59:03Z runtime error: kv_fetch miss=0.78 eviction=0.45
2026-03-13T13:59:05Z router info: fallback triggered for 12 reqs -> gptx-compact-v1
```

Chen L: My read: compaction is memory/disk-bound and it's causing IO contention -> longer KV fetch times -> batcher queue growth -> throttle rules interpret as overload -> 429s. Disabling compaction immediately reduced eviction pressure.

Sara M: Customers impacted: corp-acme-prod, fintech-satori, and med-lexa. I opened support ticket INC-5231 and notified CSMs. SRE/SEs on those accounts are aware.

Alex W: Runbook pointers: follow 'KV cache pressure' runbook -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-pressure (see steps 2a-2d). Key immediate playbook items:
- Confirm compaction job is disabled for affected pool (`kubectl get cronjobs -n infra compaction-pool-a`).
- If eviction_rate > 0.4 and queue_latency > 150ms, temporarily scale pool (horizontal) or pause background jobs.
- Fill out postmortem checklist in the runbook.

Priya K: Coverage for the next 12h:
- Primary: Priya K (local timezone EMEA 16:00-04:00 UTC) — will handle pages for Dedicated and routing.
- Secondary: Mateo R (backup for infra actions and kernel/driver escalations).
- On-call overlap: Chen L covers 18:00-22:00 UTC for troubleshooting deep-dive.
- Note: We currently have a 4h gap overnight (02:00-06:00 UTC) where oncall rota is thin due to PTO; recommended standby list added below.

Alex W: Next immediate steps for primary (Priya):
1) Monitor the 429 rate for corp-acme-prod and fintech-satori — if >0.5% for 15m, escalate to Sev1 and re-enable routing to cold fallback pool.
2) Coordinate with infra to re-run compaction with throttled IO settings (`compaction.io.bandwidth_mb=50`).
3) Confirm the ticketing updates for affected customers and schedule postmortem call with PS.

Priya K: Acknowledged. I'll put a paging rule exception so auto-escalations are suppressed during manual mitigation to avoid alert storms.

ops-bot: Reminder — scheduled maintenance window for pool-a next week: 2026-03-20 02:00-06:00 UTC.

Mateo R: Follow-ups to create (owners):
- Create infra task to make compaction safer long-term: OWNER=Chen L -> `INFRA-2984`
- Improve routing fallback logic to prefer warm cache variants: OWNER=Alex W -> `PLATFORM-4120`
- Customer postmortems & communications: OWNER=Sara M -> `CS-5231`

Chen L: I'm going to draft a short postmortem section about IO throttling limits and propose a new compaction schedule that staggers jobs across pools. Will post by EOD.

Sara M: I've messaged the CSMs and legal for corp-acme-prod and scheduled a 1:1 with them tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

Alex W: Coverage gap note (action required): we need one additional on-call volunteer for 02:00-06:00 UTC on 2026-03-14 due to PTO overlap. If no volunteer, Priya please coordinate an L1 standby from Platform team to be reachable.

Priya K: I'll ping the platform slack and ask for a volunteer. If no takers in 30m, I'll assign Mateo as standby.

Alex W: Longer-term proposals (for PD):
- Add soft backoff on compaction start when avg eviction_rate > 0.3.
- Add metric alert `kv.eviction_rate` + `batcher.queue_latency` composite alarm for early warning.

Mateo R: Quick ops note — command to re-enable compaction safely (use with care):
```
# run from infra-cluster
kubectl patch cronjob compaction-pool-a -n infra --patch '{"spec": {"suspend": false}}'
# then set throttled config
kubectl set env deployment/compaction --env=COMPACTION_IO_BANDWIDTH=50
```

Alex W: Okay team — I'm handing off. Priya, Mateo, Chen take point. I'll be reachable on DM for escalation. :thumbsup:

Priya K: Thanks Alex — taking over. Will post a 1h status update or sooner if anything changes. :eyes:
